title: Persona Prompting as a Lens on LLM Social Reasoning
benchmark_measurement: The study measured how prompting Large Language Models with personas based on religious identity (among other demographic attributes) affects their performance on hate speech detection, commonsense reasoning, and sentiment analysis tasks. This included evaluating changes in classification accuracy, rationale selection quality, and the model's tendency to over-flag content as harmful.
findings: Prompting with religious personas, as with other demographic attributes, had varied effects. For hate speech detection, some religious personas improved classification for certain models (e.g., Atheist persona for Mistral-Medium) but often degraded the quality of the selected rationales. Models showed significant disagreement in their predictions when prompted with different religious personas, with the 'Religion' and 'Political View' categories showing the most divergence. Furthermore, the study found that simulated personas (including religious ones) often fail to align with their real-world counterparts and that models exhibit consistent biases regardless of the persona prompt, such as a strong tendency to over-flag content as harmful.
